instruments.title: A trough zither, with a hollow body and a curved base, ornamented at each end with concave cut-outs at the corners and incised grooves. There is a conical, rod-like handle at one end. The zither is strung with a single string made from fibre; it is strung across the body of the zither six times through holes at both ends of the trough. The string has come undone at one end. There are three sets of sheet iron squares attached the bottom of the body of the zither, to act as jingles. According to the collector, it would have been held in both hands and played with the thumbs.

A pair of rattles. Each consisting of three seed pods filled with seeds and threaded onto a stick. Two of these sticks are tied together with plant fibre string to make a wearable rattle. There are intersecting lines centrally carved on some seed pods. Worn on the ankles by women and girls when dancing.
A pair of flat square rattles made of plant fibre and bound at opposite ends. Filled with loose seeds that make a sound when moved. Beaten by girls in dances.

Two whistles, made from scraped and cleaned kaffir oranges. Both are spherical in shape and have one large central hole and one smaller side hole. Used on night marshes to the coast to frighten wild beasts away from the path, the first and last person for the group of travellers being provided with an instrument.

Mörser mit Stößel für Mais

A basketry purse, roughly rectangular in shape, with a cover that slots over the opening. It is woven from plant fibre in various shades of brown, the different colours used to create interwoven patterns. It has a long string, made from twisted plant fibre, attached to the two upper corners that allow the purse to be worn around the neck.

Chief's wooden headrest. Carved in relief from a single piece of wood. Curved head piece attached to an arched support with a geometric base. Beneath the head piece on each side are small semicircular and rectangular protrusions. Some sections coloured darker brown.

A wooden drinking cup used by chiefs. It has a rounded body that slopes up to an upright rim, a conical base, a looped handle on one side of the body and a small, triangular boss on the other side. The outside of the cup has been darkened, and the body is decorated with carved triangles.

A drinking cup made from a coconut shell with an ornate geometric design of bands and squares carved into the outside. It has a long, cylindrical wooden handle with carved decoration, that goes through a hole in the side of the cup. Pyrography has been used to decorate these carved sections.

A wooden food bowl with a rounded base. The rim and outer surface have been darkened using pyrography, and a design of grooved triangles and a band with four sections of small triangles has been carved into the outside.
A gourd water vessel. Hollowed out gourd with opening at top. Dried corn cob used as a stopper. Plant fibre string tied around waist.

Spoon carved from wood, with a teardrop-shaped bowl and a long rectangular handle with a widened section at the end. The upper side of the handle and the rim of the bowl have been darkened using a flame, and there is a small motif of three short lines that has been impressed into the bowl with pyropgraphy. There is a hole in the end of the spoon's handle, possibly for suspension.
Spoon carved from wood, used for stirring soup. It is decorated with pyrography around the edge of the bowl and along the handle.
A wooden hoe. A very wide blade with central midrib and curved end. Blade fitted into a wooden haft with the tang bent to secure in place.
A circular winnowing basket with a wide mouth, sloping sides and a flat base. Coiled basket with a woven in linear pattern. Used for separating the chaff from grain.
Rectangular basket with a cover and loop for suspension. Decorated with intersecting diagonal lines of a darker colour. Used for carrying food.

Small bag or purse covered with netted glass beadwork. Woven plant fibre bag with plaited handle integrated into the sides; decoration of crosses in darker plant fibre. The bag and handle are covered in netted beadwork with a diamond motif in white, pink/red, black, yellow and navy blue. The handle features a chevron design in the same colours.

A beer palm wine strainer, consisting of a long basketry funnel made from plant fibre. The wider, open end is rolled over and has a plant fibre fringe. There is a plaited plant fibre loop attached the narrower, closed end.
A water gourd, with a circular hole in the top that would have been plugged with a corn husk (however, this has now fallen into the gourd). There is a string of twisted plant around the neck.

A chief's drinking cup, carved from wood, with a rounded base, everted rim, and looped handle. The outside of the cup has been darkened using a flame, and there is an incised line with triangular sections carved around the middle.

Small lidded globular basket (.1), coiled construction with small decorative protrusions on sides and lid. The lid is round and slots over the rim, and is connected to the body of the basket with a short strap. There is a longer looped strap attached to the basket either side of the rim, likely for suspension or wearing. Inside the basket there is wild, unprocessed cotton (.2).

A comb carved from wood. It has five pointed prongs, and a square handle with two inward-pointing triangular projections at the top. The handle is decorated with an incised geometric design on both sides.

A wooden comb, with five pointed prongs and a square handle with two rectangular projections at the top. The handle is decorated with an incised geometric design on one side, and a incised animal, likely a hyena or similar, on the other.

A comb, carved from wood, with five pointed prongs and a square handle with two inward-pointing triangular projections at the top. The handle is decorated with an incised geometric design on one side, and an incised motif on the other.
Composite comb with eight pointed wooden prongs, the tops fastened together with copper wire lashings. The four inner prongs are shorter at the top, so the two outer prongs at each side project out.

A drinking cup made from a coconut shell with an ornate geometric design of bands and circles carved into the outside. It has a long, cylindrical wooden handle with carved decoration, that goes through a hole in the side of the cup. Pyrography has been used to decorate these carved sections.

A basketry purse, roughly rectangular in shape, with a cover that slots over the opening. It is woven from plant fibre, and it has a long string, made from twisted plant fibre, attached to the two upper corners that allow the purse to be worn around the neck.

A wooden drinking cup, used by chiefs. It is cylindrical, rounded at the bottom of the cup section, with a stepped cylindrical base. There is a handle out to one side that consists of three horizontal bars, all connected with a vertical bar. Sections of the handle and base have been darkened, likely using a flame.

A chief's drinking cup, carved from wood, with a rounded base, everted rim, and looped handle. The outside of the cup has been darkened using a flame, and there is an incised line with triangular sections carved around the middle.

Wooden headrest. Carved in relief from a single piece of wood and stained dark brown. Small upward curving head piece with pointed ends. Supported by a long, rectangular middle section with decorative notches cut along each side. Hemispherical shape at bottom with flat base.

jewelry.title: 21 small bangles, worn by women and children, strung on a split twig to be taken to the market. Each is made from a loop of elephant hair, tightly wrapped with metal wire. Ten are wrapped with a bright silver wire (likely aluminium) and the other 11 are wrapped in a dark grey/bronze wire (likely corroded copper alloy).

Ten leg ornaments, worn below the knees. Each is made from a loop of elephant hair, tightly wrapped with metal wire, likely copper or a copper alloy such as brass. One is much thinner than the other nine.

garment.title: Chief's headdress. Circular head piece made from glass beads threaded on plant fibre string. Arranged in triangular and linear patterns with black, green, white, yellow, red and blue coloured beads. Also word by the Chief's wife when she has given birth to a son.

arms.title: A musical bow, with gourd resonator and a metal wire string. The bow is made from wood and curves in at both ends. The string, likely made from brass or another copper alloy, is tied onto the bow at both ends. The resonator is made from half of a dark orange/brown gourd, and is attached to the bow with metal wire.

Iron axe with wooden handle. The handle is carved into a double rounded shape at the top. The blade is narrow, narrowing towards the tang. The handle has a circular cross-section and is tapered towards the terminal.
Simple wooden bow with tapered ends. Twisted hide string tied in tension to both ends of the shaft. The string is made from two parts tied together in the middle.
Spear with leaf shaped iron blade, central midrib and four cut outs and with dark red on one side. Attached with iron socket to cylindrical wooden shaft with spherical end. Carried for self defence.

Musical bow with a brass wire string. The bow is wooden, and curves round at either end. There is a small notch in both ends to keep the string in place. The string has broken and some of it is missing. The bow should also have a gourd resonator (E 1916.31.19 B) but it is missing.
Arrow with a wooden shaft and notched terminal. The head made of iron; large and leaf shaped with a faint midrib. Bound at the tang with plant fibre.
Arrow with a wooden shaft and large feather fletchings. The head made of iron; angular in shape with barbed shoulders and a long tang. Tip is bent. Bound at the tang and fletching with plant fibre.
Arrow with a wooden shaft and and integrated barbed head. The terminal is notched.

other.title: Two flexible girdles made of elephant's hair, worn over loin cloths by both men and women. The elephants hair endows the wearer with strength. The loop of hair is wrapped with silver metal fine wire, and there is a small decorative section in the middle where the wire has been tightly coiled before it is wrapped around.
A rectangular wooden panel from across the bottom of a doorway to a house. The surface is carved with an ornate pattern.

A wooden utensil used by women for tasting soup, taken from an old house. It has a long handle with a flat top and a squared end, and a long, narrow, shallow bowl carved into the other end. The top of the handle and the sides of the bowl have been darkened with pyrography.

A wooden utensil used by women for tasting soup, taken from an old house. It has a long cylindrical handle with carved decoration, with a very small flattened section at one end for tasting the soup. The other end has been craved into a spike so that the utensil can be stood up in the earth.
